opening.headline: If you are using AI results without knowing whether they are correct or incorrect, you need a standard to determine which results must be confirmed.
body: The AI's answers have smooth sentences and confident tone. So it's easy to feel like the content is accurate, but smooth sentences and accurate content are two different things. Even if the definitions, dates, quotations, and figures are wrong, the tone can still be the same.

In this class, we will first organize the concepts of hallucination and uncertainty that refer to this phenomenon, and then follow the process of verifying answers with incorrect sources. We then look at how model developers design to deal with uncertainty, and then distinguish between the types of results that need to be verified using two examples: legal citations and statistical figures.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can identify results that require verification

screens.title: I am writing this without knowing if it is right or wrong.
screens.lead: First, let's think about the scene when we received the AI answer. Read the information below and think about which parts you can trust.

visual.alt: A scene with a confident AI answer card on the left and a question mark card asking if there is evidence on the right.

paragraphs: AI's answers are usually well-written and confident. Because the tone answers the question directly, it is easy for the reader to accept that the content is accurate.

But as OpenAI's help acknowledges, models can sound confident even while giving wrong answers. Examples include incorrect definitions or dates, non-existent quotes or studies, or overconfident answers to vague or complex questions. Since correct and incorrect words are spoken in the same tone, it is impossible to distinguish them based on tone alone.
So, when using AI for work, you need standards to determine what results you must check. The purpose of this class is to create that standard.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: In how many parts of the AI answer I received did I personally check the evidence? You will be able to identify the parts you need to check at the end of class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall my experience writing AI results without verification.

screens.title: Experience writing without confirmation
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Have you ever experienced a problem with AI results written without verification?
items.answer: It is not uncommon to experience citing different figures or non-existent data. This often happens not because the AI ​​is particularly careless, but because it is used without checking. Rather than feeling embarrassed about your experience, it may be helpful to think about what type of information gave you trouble.

items.prompt: What kind of information was the result? Was it a definition, a date, a figure, a citation?
items.answer: Information that is easy to be wrong and has a big impact if wrong has something in common. It must be specific, accurate, and can be verified by searching. In this lesson, we organize them into types of results that require verification.

items.prompt: Do you think you can trust it if AI cites the source?
items.answer: The fact that a source is attached only makes verification easier, but does not guarantee that the content is correct. A person must open and check whether the source is real and contains what is claimed.

screens.outro: Let's start the demonstration by naming the phenomenon that we are experiencing.

screens.title: Hallucination and uncertainty
screens.lead: The following cards explain five concepts you need to know when reading AI results. Selecting a card flips it over, and selecting the right arrow moves to the next card.

cards.back: This is a phenomenon in which a model makes something that is not true seem plausible. Typical examples include incorrect definitions or dates, non-existent quotes, studies and sources, and overconfident answers to vague and complex questions. The model is not intentionally deceiving, but an error that occurs when it answers based on the patterns of the learned data.

The model can demonstrate high confidence even in incorrect answers. The fact that your tone is confident does not mean it is accurate. So when evaluating an answer, look at the evidence, not the tone.

The model is trained with data up to a certain point in time, so without tools it cannot reflect what happened after that. When asking about recent events or changed information, you should check whether tools such as search are turned on, and even if you use a tool, you should open the basis for the answer.

Models may not be able to obtain information from certain websites due to technical issues, paid subscription barriers, or site access restrictions. If an answer is created without reading the required material, the answer may be lacking evidence.

Depending on your plan, tools like search, data analysis, and in-depth investigation help improve accuracy. Search helps you get answers with citations, data analysis helps you make accurate calculations, and in-depth research helps you get answers that synthesize multiple sources. Still, the final confirmation is up to you. Just because the tool is turned on doesn't mean the results are correct, so check quotes and figures in the same way for responses you use the tool.

screens.outro: Now that you understand the concept, let's follow along to see how sources actually verify incorrect answers.

screens.title: Process of verifying answers with incorrect sources
screens.lead: Follow the process of verifying a single citation in the AI answer step by step with the arrow to the right.

visual.alt: Verification flowchart in which the quotation in the AI answer changes from unconfirmed to being confirmed to not actually being confirmed.
labels: Step 1: Search to see if the document actually exists
Step 2: If there is a link, open it directly
Step 3: If the document does not exist or the content is different, do not write it
Step 4: Find evidence again with reliable data

steps.title: Find and mark citations
steps.body: Suppose the AI answer contains the quote According to Report A. Don't trust a sentence just because it's smooth, mark it as something that needs confirmation. Status at this time is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Step 1: Search to see if the document actually exists
steps.body: Search to see if a document called Report A actually exists. Since hallucinations make non-existent studies or sources plausible, they should not be trusted just because the name sounds plausible.

steps.title: Step 2: If there is a link, open it directly
steps.body: If there's a link in the answer, open it to see if it actually contains the content. The same goes for citations provided by search or research functions. The status is being checked until you open it.

steps.title: Step 3: If the document does not exist or the content is different, do not write it
steps.body: If the document does not exist or the content is different, the citation is considered made up and will not be used. The status indicator changes to Invisible. Even if there are other similar documents, they will not be used as a basis for what the AI ​​says.

steps.title: Step 4: Find evidence again with reliable data
steps.body: If the claim itself is necessary, find new evidence from reliable sources and record the source. This way, the AI's answers go into the report, linked to confirmed evidence.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen one verification, let's see how model developers design it to deal with uncertainty.

screens.title: AI that speaks of uncertainty
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare what the two companies' documents say about uncertainty.

tabs.label: OpenAI Model Spec
tabs.body: OpenAI's Model Specification guides you to consider uncertainty, uncover assumptions, and ask confirmatory questions when appropriate. When uncertainty remains, make reasonable assumptions, but avoid taking large, unauthorized risks. If you proceed with guesses, make sure to clearly state the assumptions and uncertainties in your final answer. We believe that execution errors can be reduced by efforts to avoid errors in facts and inferences and expressions of uncertainty.

tabs.label: Claude constitution
tabs.body: Anthropic's Claude constitution cites calibrated uncertainty as a form of honesty. Adjust your level of certainty based on evidence and sound reasoning, admit that you don't know what you don't know, and avoid conveying more or less confidence than you actually have.

tabs.label: user's share
tabs.body: What both documents say is that models are designed to reveal uncertainty. But models don't always do that, and there remain cases where they confidently tell us the wrong answer. So the final confirmation must be done by the user.

screens.outro: Let us confirm from examples citing laws that even if the model speaks of uncertainty, verification is done by humans.

screens.title: Commentary: Verification of law citations
screens.lead: The instructor explains step by step the process of verifying a draft report that cites laws and regulations. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: The draft report prepared by AI includes a citation to the law stating that this plan is possible under certain provisions. Since this is a sentence with legal effect, whether this quote is correct determines the credibility of the entire report.

steps.title: Step 1: Mark the items that need to be correct
steps.body: Mark items that need to be accurate, such as law name, section number, date, and what applies. Because these items are specific, it is easy to be wrong, and even if just one difference is made, the conclusion will change.

steps.title: Step 2: Find the text in official legal documents
steps.body: Look for the relevant provisions directly in the official statutory material, not in the AI's explanation. The original text is used as the standard, not summary articles or blogs. At this time, number errors can be filtered out by searching by the name and content of the law rather than the article number provided by AI.

steps.title: Step 3: Compare the condolences and explanations
steps.body: Compare the contents of the condolence sentence one by one to see if it matches the AI's explanation. Check to see if any conditions are attached that are not present in the clause, or conversely, important exceptions are missing.

steps.title: Step 4: Check separately the parts that are difficult to be sure of
steps.body: The revision and scope of application may change after the model is trained and are difficult to be certain of. Please check separately to see if it is currently in effect.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: What AI did in this case was to speed up the draft. Quotations with legal effect must be confirmed in the original text. AI's explanations are used as a guide to where to look, not as evidence. If you follow this order, your report will not be wrong even if the AI ​​is wrong.

screens.outro: Now that we're done with the high-risk quotes, let's solve cases where numbers appear in the same way.

screens.title: Commentary: Verification of statistical figures
screens.lead: When you select an underlined passage in the AI summary below, you'll see instructions on how to access each passage.

data.text: AI Summary: The domestic online education market has grown from As of 2023 to Average annual growth of 23%, which represents Findings from Report A. However, Not all industries grow at the same rate.

marks.note: Figures are meaningful when accompanied by a source, base year, and definition. You must check in the original text whether 23% is based on sales or number of users, and whether it is an annual average or a single year.
If the base year is different, the same numbers have different meanings. Compare it directly with the corresponding year column in the table in the original text.
Open the sourced report directly to check that the numbers, units, and years match. If the source is missing or incorrect, it will not be written in the report or marked as unfounded.

marks.span: Not all industries grow at the same rate
marks.note: Sentences that generalize also need to be checked. These sentences are often added without any basis, so look for the content in the original text. If it cannot be found, the sentence is omitted or marked as unfounded.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed that the verification method is the same in both cases, let us summarize the types of results that require verification.

screens.title: Criteria for selecting results that require verification
screens.lead: We will organize what we have seen so far into one standard. Please read and think about which of the results I am writing about applies to you.

paragraphs: AI can say something incorrect in a confident tone. Therefore, information that must be specific and accurate, such as definitions, dates, figures, quotations, and laws, and that has a large impact if incorrect, is classified as a result that requires verification.

Just because a source is attached doesn't mean it's true. You must personally open and check whether the cited material actually exists and contains what you claim. AI results are drafts and not final evidence.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: A confident tone and accurate content are two different things. Check the original text starting with specific and influential information. Please record the evidence you have verified.

glossary.def: This is a phenomenon in which a model makes information that is not factual or a source that does not exist seem plausible.
The answer can be wrong. A good answer reveals what you don't know.
This is specific information that can have a big impact if incorrect, such as definitions, dates, figures, citations, and laws.
This involves opening and comparing the cited material to see if it actually exists and contains what was claimed.

misconceptions.myth: If your tone of voice is confident, it is accurate.
misconceptions.fact: Confidence and reliability are two different things. The model can also say incorrect answers in the same tone.

misconceptions.myth: If the source is attached, it is true.
misconceptions.fact: You must verify for yourself whether the source actually exists and what it claims. Sources only make verification easier.

misconceptions.myth: If the tool is turned on, no confirmation is needed.
misconceptions.fact: Tools like search and in-depth research increase accuracy, but providers advise you to verify important information with reliable sources.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: AI can confidently say something is wrong.
Definitions, dates, figures, citations, and laws are representative types that require verification.
Even if the source is attached, open it and check it yourself.
AI results are drafts and are not final.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Which of the AI results am I using these days without verification?

checks.q: The AI answer has the quote 'According to Report A'. What should I check first?
options: Search to see if report A actually exists.
The sentence is smooth, so use it as is.
If you ask the same question again and get the same answer, it is considered true.
Check whether the report name is plausible.
checks.explain: Hallucination makes non-existent citations or sources plausible. You must personally verify that the cited document actually exists and that the content is correct.

wrong.1: Smooth sentences and accurate content are two different things.
wrong.2: Even if the same answer is repeated, the basis is not confirmed.
wrong.3: Even if the name sounds good, we don't know if it's real or not.

checks.intro: Check out the verification process you just saw for yourself. Results are not recorded, and commentary appears immediately after you select an option.

checks.q: Put the procedure for verifying legal citations in order.
items: Indicate items that must be accurate (statutory name, article number, date)
Find the relevant provisions directly in official legal documents
Compare the contents of the condolences and AI's explanation to see if they match.
Check separately for parts that are difficult to be sure, such as whether or not there has been a revision and the scope of application.
checks.explain: First, we select the items to be checked, then find and compare the original text, and finally, AI supplements the parts that are difficult to be sure about.
checks.intro: Think about the order in which you would verify legal citations and arrange them. Results are not recorded.
